title: Regulations Relating to Banks (under Banks Act 94 of 1990)
sourceNote: Regulations Relating to Banks issued under section 90 of the Banks Act 94 of 1990. Published in Government Gazette No. 35950 of 12 December 2012. Incorporates Basel III capital adequacy requirements as adapted for South Africa by the Prudential Authority.

sections.title: Objective of Regulations and completeness of information

subsections.heading: reg1.p
subsections.text: 1. Objective of Regulations and completeness of information

subsections.heading: reg1.1
subsections.text: (1) The objective of these Regulations is to provide for the establishment of basic principles relating to the maintenance of effective risk management by banks and controlling companies, with due allowance for the ancillary objective that the benefits derived by banks and controlling companies from compliance with these Regulations exceed the costs entailed by such compliance.

subsections.heading: reg1.2
subsections.text: (2) All information required to be reported in the forms prescribed in these Regulations shall be reflected against the appropriate items and in the columns specified in the forms. For example, subject to the provisions of regulation 2, all liabilities consisting of claims relating to and all assets arising from the business of the reporting bank shall be included against the appropriate liability or asset items in the relevant columns provided.

subsections.heading: reg1.3
subsections.text: (3) Upon request, an analysis of any information or item furnished or appearing in any of the forms referred to in subregulation (2) shall be made available to the Registrar within a reasonable period of time.

sections.title: Management accounts as basis for the completion of returns

subsections.heading: reg2.p
subsections.text: 2. Management accounts as basis for the completion of returns

subsections.heading: reg2.1
subsections.text: (1) Unless expressly otherwise provided in the Act or these Regulations, all the prescribed returns shall reflect the management accounts presented to the management and/or board of directors of a bank or controlling company in the sense that the said returns—

subsections.heading: reg2.1.a
subsections.text: shall be prepared using the same principles used in the preparation of such management accounts and/or board reports;

subsections.heading: reg2.1.b
subsections.text: shall be easily reconcilable to such management accounts and/or board reports.

subsections.heading: reg2.2
subsections.text: (2) In the event of a conflict between the instructions, directives and interpretations relating to the completion of the returns, as prescribed in these Regulations, and the manner in which the management accounts of the bank or controlling company concerned are completed, the basis and composition of amounts disclosed in such management accounts shall after consultation with the Registrar be presented to the Registrar for approval, provided that in all cases the aggregate amount of the relevant amounts disclosed shall agree or easily be reconcilable.

sections.title: Financial Reporting Standards

subsections.heading: reg3.p
subsections.text: 3. Financial Reporting Standards

subsections.heading: reg3.1
subsections.text: (1) Subject to the provisions of regulation 9, unless expressly otherwise provided in the Act or these Regulations, all the relevant prescribed returns shall be prepared in accordance with Financial Reporting Standards issued from time to time, with additional disclosure when required, provided that in the absence of a specific Financial Reporting Standard and an approved interpretation reference shall be made to the relevant pronouncements of the International Accounting Standards Board. In virtually all circumstances the appropriate application of Financial Reporting Standards results in returns and information that provide a fair presentation of the financial position, the results of operations and the relevant risk positions of the relevant bank or controlling company.

subsections.heading: reg3.2
subsections.text: (2) Unless—

subsections.heading: reg3.2.a
subsections.text: specifically otherwise provided in these Regulations; or

subsections.heading: reg3.2.b
subsections.text:
on prior application, the Registrar authorised a deviation from such policy,
the same accounting policy applied by a bank or controlling company in the compilation of its annual financial statements shall be applied by such bank or controlling company in the compilation of the prescribed returns required to be furnished to the Registrar in terms of the Act and these Regulations.

subsections.heading: reg3.3
subsections.text: (3) In the event of a deviation in the compilation of the prescribed returns required to be furnished by a bank or controlling company to the Registrar in terms of the Act and these Regulations from the accounting policy applied by such a bank or controlling company in the compilation of its annual financial statements, as envisaged in subregulation (2), the said returns shall be easily reconcilable to the said annual financial statements.

subsections.heading: reg3.4
subsections.text: (4) When a bank or controlling company, in accordance with the relevant requirements contained in Financial Reporting Standards issued from time to time, wishes to implement or adopt any fair value option or approach in respect of financial instruments, the said bank or controlling company—

subsections.heading: reg3.4.a
reg3.4.b
subsections.text: shall at all times, in form and in substance, comply with any relevant criteria or requirements contained in the relevant Financial Reporting Standard;

subsections.heading: reg3.4.c
subsections.text: shall duly document its application of the fair value option or approach and all relevant or related matters;

subsections.heading: reg3.4.d

sections.title: Certification and rendition of returns

subsections.heading: reg4.p
subsections.text: 4. Certification and rendition of returns

subsections.heading: reg4.1
subsections.text: (1) Irrespective whether a return is rendered on a prescribed form or by means of an electronic facility, the chief executive officer, chief accounting officer and executive officer responsible for the relevant reporting bank or controlling company's compliance with the Financial Intelligence Centre Act, 2001 (Act No. 38 of 2001), as amended (FICA), shall sign and certify the prescribed form BA 099 in respect of each return indicated on the said form.

subsections.heading: reg4.2
subsections.text: (2) Every set of returns rendered simultaneously, as mentioned in subregulation (1), shall be accompanied by a duly completed, signed and certified form BA 099.

subsections.heading: reg4.3
subsections.text: (3) When the chief executive officer, chief accounting officer or executive officer responsible for compliance with FICA is not available to sign a completed form BA 099, the officer performing the relevant function shall sign the said form in an acting capacity and not on behalf of the absent officer, and the normal office of the officer so acting shall be clearly stated on the form BA 099.

subsections.heading: reg4.4
subsections.text: (4) The furnishing of the returns referred to in these Regulations, whether by way of the completion of the prescribed forms or by electronic means, shall be done at the intervals indicated in Chapter II and Chapter VI of these Regulations, and such returns shall be forwarded to the Registrar at the address set out in regulation 6(1).

subsections.heading: reg4.5
subsections.text: (5) A reporting bank or controlling company shall submit every appropriate, duly completed form prescribed in Chapter II and Chapter VI of these Regulations, reflecting the required particulars relating to the business conducted by it in the Republic.

subsections.heading: reg4.6
subsections.text: (6) A reporting bank or controlling company shall, apart from the forms referred to in subregulation (5), submit every appropriate, duly completed form prescribed in Chapter II and Chapter VI of these Regulations, reflecting the required particulars relating to the relevant business conducted by it, other than the business referred to in subregulation (5), through the medium of an agency or in respect of a branch, a subsidiary company or a relevant associate contemplated in regulation 45(2)(b) in each country elsewhere in the world.

subsections.heading: reg4.7
subsections.text: (7) Unless otherwise indicated, all returns shall be completed in either the currency of the country in which the banking or relevant business is being conducted or in the currency in which the banking or relevant business is officially reported, whichever is applicable.

subsections.heading: reg4.8
subsections.text: (8) When completing the returns in respect of banking business conducted outside the Republic, the definitions and interpretation of items used in these Regulations shall be applied to the circumstances prevailing in each relevant country and any difficulty experienced or uncertainty in this regard shall be referred to the Registrar for an appropriate directive.

sections.title: Failure or inability to comply with the provisions of the Regulations

subsections.heading: reg5.p
subsections.text: 5. Failure or inability to comply with the provisions of the Regulations

subsections.heading: reg5.1
subsections.text: (1) Subject to the provisions of section 74 of the Act, a bank, controlling company, branch or branch of a bank that fails or is unable to comply with a provision of these Regulations shall report its failure or inability to comply in writing to the Registrar, stating the reasons for such failure or inability to comply.

subsections.heading: reg5.2
subsections.text: (2) The Registrar may summarily take action under the Act or these Regulations against a bank, controlling company, branch or branch of a bank referred to in subregulation (1) or, if in the circumstances the Registrar deems it fit to do so, condone the said failure or inability and, subject to such conditions as may be specified in writing, afford the institution concerned an opportunity to comply with the relevant provision within a specified period.

sections.title: General

subsections.heading: reg6.p
subsections.text: 6. General

subsections.heading: reg6.1
subsections.text: (1) Forms to be completed and submitted in terms of these Regulations can be obtained from the Reserve Bank, Office for Banks, P O Box 8432, Pretoria, 0001, and shall be completed and submitted in accordance with the relevant instructions, directives and interpretations contained in the applicable chapters of these Regulations.

subsections.heading: reg6.2
subsections.text: (2) A bank or controlling company is not obliged to use the forms provided by the Office for Banks, but any reproduction used by the said bank or controlling company shall in all respects correspond to the prescribed forms.

subsections.heading: reg6.3
subsections.text: (3) Additional facilities are provided by the Office for Banks for the rendition by a bank or controlling company of the required information in the prescribed statements and returns by electronic means, and further details in this regard may be obtained from the said Office for Banks.

chapters.title: Chapter II — Financial, Risk-Based and Other Related Returns

sections.title: List of forms prescribed in respect of financial, risk-based and other related returns
sections.summary: Lists all prescribed BA forms (BA 099, BA 100, BA 110–BA 700) together with the institution type required to submit each form, the submission interval (daily, monthly, quarterly, six-monthly, or annually), and the deadline after period-end — ranging from 2 business days for the daily BA 325 to 90 days for annual consolidated returns.

sections.title: Calculation of averages
sections.summary: Prescribes that, unless otherwise specified, averages required in the forms shall be calculated as the average of the daily amounts outstanding during the reporting month, with specific rules for items such as reserve bank notes, subsidiary coin, and level one high-quality liquid assets.

sections.title: Gross balances
sections.summary: Requires that, unless expressly otherwise provided, all items in the prescribed returns reflect gross balances without netting of assets against liabilities or income against expenses, except where set-off is specifically permitted under regulation 13.

sections.title: Maturity classification
sections.summary: Prescribes the maturity buckets to be used across the prescribed forms (overnight, 1–7 days, 8 days–1 month, 1–3 months, 3–6 months, 6–12 months, 1–3 years, 3–5 years, over 5 years, unspecified) and rules for classifying instruments into those buckets based on original contractual maturity.

sections.title: Balance sheet — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly balance sheet (Form BA 100)
sections.summary: Provides detailed directives and interpretations for completing the monthly balance sheet return (Form BA 100), covering classification of assets and liabilities, treatment of accrued interest, off-balance sheet items, interbank positions, and reconciliation to general ledger; content is confidential and not available for public inspection.

sections.title: Credit risk — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return concerning credit risk (Form BA 200)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly credit risk return (Form BA 200), including the standardised approach and internal ratings-based (IRB) approach for measuring credit risk exposures, risk-weight tables by asset class and external credit assessment, credit risk mitigation techniques, counterparty credit risk methods (current exposure, standardised, and internal model), securitisation exposures, and the calculation of risk-weighted exposure and capital requirements; the regulation incorporates the Basel III credit risk framework as adapted by the Prudential Authority and runs to approximately 30,000 lines including extensive numerical tables.

sections.title: Credit risk — Directives and interpretations for completion of quarterly return concerning credit risk (Form BA 210)
sections.summary: Prescribes the quarterly credit risk return (Form BA 210) covering credit risk mitigation, restructured credit exposures, credit risk classification and impairment under the standardised approach, credit concentration risk, large exposures to a single person, watch-list exposures, and connected/related-party lending.

sections.title: Credit risk — Directives and interpretations for completion of six-monthly return concerning credit risk (Form BA 220)
sections.summary: Prescribes the six-monthly credit risk return (Form BA 220) covering assets bought-in by the reporting bank, including the nature, carrying amount, and capital requirements applicable to such assets.

sections.title: Liquidity risk — Directives, definitions and interpretations for completion of monthly return concerning liquidity risk (Form BA 300)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly liquidity risk return (Form BA 300), implementing the Basel III Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) and Net Stable Funding Ratio (NSFR) frameworks; defines high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) and their haircuts, specifies run-off rate assumptions for various liability categories under a 30-day stress scenario, and sets out the stable funding factors for the NSFR; includes detailed maturity-ladder tables across currency buckets and funding concentration analysis.

sections.title: Minimum reserve balance and liquid assets — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return (Form BA 310)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly minimum reserve balance and liquid assets return (Form BA 310), implementing section 72(1) of the Banks Act requirement that a bank hold an average daily amount of level one high-quality liquid assets equal to at least 5 per cent of its prescribed liabilities, calculated in accordance with any Notice issued by the Governor of the Reserve Bank under section 10A of the South African Reserve Bank Act.

sections.title: Market risk (position risk) — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return concerning market risk (Form BA 320)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly market risk return (Form BA 320), implementing the Basel II/III standardised approach for position risk capital requirements covering interest rate risk in the trading book (specific and general risk for debt instruments), equity position risk, foreign exchange risk, and commodity risk; includes the internal models approach (VaR-based) subject to prior Registrar approval and rules for the trading-book/banking-book boundary.

sections.title: Daily return: selected risk exposure arising from trading and treasury activities (Form BA 325)
sections.summary: Prescribes the daily trading and treasury risk return (Form BA 325), requiring banks to report before 09:00 on the following business day the aggregate notional value and fair value of all trading positions and treasury exposures, including derivative instruments, with breakdown by risk category and instrument type.

sections.title: Interest-rate risk in the banking book — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return (Form BA 330)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly interest rate risk in the banking book (IRRBB) return (Form BA 330), requiring banks to report the sensitivity of net interest income and economic value of equity to standardised interest rate shock scenarios across currency buckets and maturity bands, and to hold appropriate capital for material IRRBB exposures as directed by the Registrar.

sections.title: Equity risk in the banking book — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return (Form BA 340)
sections.verbatimOpening:
31. Equity risk in the banking book - Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return concerning equity risk in the banking book (Form BA 340)

(1) The content of the relevant return is confidential and not available for inspection by the public.

(2) The purpose of the return, amongst other things, is to determine the nature and extent of the reporting bank's exposure to investment risk arising from equity positions and other relevant investments or instruments held in its banking book.

(3) Criteria relating to categorisation of equity exposures held in a bank's banking book: Based on the economic substance and not the legal form of an instrument, and irrespective whether or not the said instrument makes provision for a voting right, for the purposes of these Regulations equity exposures held in a bank's banking book—
(a) shall include—
(i) any direct ownership interest in the assets and income of a commercial or financial institution;
(ii) any indirect ownership interest in the assets and income of a commercial or financial institution, including (A) a derivative instrument held, which derivative instrument is linked to an equity interest; (B) any instrument or interest held in a corporation, partnership, limited liability company or other type of enterprise that issues ownership interests and which in turn principally is engaged in the business of investing in equity instruments;
(iii) any instrument that (A) is not redeemable, that is, the return of invested funds can be achieved only by way of the sale of the relevant instrument, the sale of the rights to the relevant investment or the liquidation of the issuer of the relevant instrument; (B) does not constitute an obligation of the issuer of the instrument; (C) entitles the holder of or investor in the said instrument to a residual claim in respect of the assets or income of the issuer of the said instrument.
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly equity risk in the banking book return (Form BA 340), requiring banks to categorise banking-book equity exposures (publicly traded, non-publicly traded, equity in funds), calculate capital requirements under the simple risk weight method (300% for publicly traded equities, 400% for all other equities), and disclose equity investment policies and the use of any internal models approach subject to Registrar approval.

sections.title: Derivative instruments — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return (Form BA 350)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly derivative instruments return (Form BA 350), capturing turnover (notional entered during the month) and open positions (notional and fair value of unexpired contracts) broken down by risk category (credit, interest rate, foreign exchange, equity, commodity), by instrument type (forward, swap, option), and distinguishing OTC from exchange-traded derivatives and credit derivatives from other derivatives.

sections.title: Operational risk — Directives and interpretations for completion of six-monthly return (Form BA 400)
sections.summary: Prescribes the six-monthly operational risk return (Form BA 400), implementing the Basel II/III basic indicator approach (15% of average annual gross income over three years), standardised approach (business-line beta factors ranging from 12%–18%), and advanced measurement approach (internal loss data, external data, scenario analysis, and business environment factors) for calculating operational risk capital requirements.

sections.title: Operational risk — Directives and interpretations for completion of six-monthly return (Form BA 410)
sections.summary: Prescribes the six-monthly supplementary operational risk return (Form BA 410), requiring banks using the standardised or advanced measurement approach to report gross loss amounts, recovery amounts, and number of loss events by Basel operational risk event-type category and business line for the reporting six-month period.

sections.title: Securitisation schemes — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return (Form BA 500)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly securitisation return (Form BA 500), covering both traditional and synthetic securitisations and resecuritisations, the calculation of capital requirements for retained or purchased securitisation exposures under the ratings-based approach, the supervisory formula approach, and the internal assessment approach, and disclosure of credit enhancements, liquidity facilities, and the bank's role as originator, sponsor, or investor.

sections.title: Consolidated supervision — Directives and interpretations for completion of quarterly consolidated return (Form BA 600)
sections.summary: Prescribes the quarterly consolidated supervision return (Form BA 600), requiring banks and controlling companies subject to section 52 of the Banks Act to report consolidated capital adequacy, risk-weighted exposures, and intra-group exposures across the consolidated group, including all subsidiary banks, non-bank entities, and relevant associates.

sections.title: Consolidated supervision — Directives for completion of six-monthly return concerning foreign operations of South African banks (Form BA 610)
sections.summary: Prescribes the six-monthly return (Form BA 610) for South African banks' foreign operations, requiring disclosure of country-by-country assets, liabilities, capital, and risk-weighted exposures of foreign branches and relevant subsidiaries, and compliance with host-country prudential requirements.

sections.title: Capital adequacy and leverage — Directives and interpretations for completion of monthly return (Form BA 700)
sections.summary: Prescribes the monthly capital adequacy and leverage return (Form BA 700), implementing the Basel III capital adequacy framework for South Africa: defines qualifying capital components (Common Equity Tier 1 — CET1, Additional Tier 1 — AT1, and Tier 2), regulatory deductions and adjustments, minimum capital ratio requirements (CET1 4.5%, Tier 1 6.0%, Total Capital 9.5% plus conservation buffer 2.5% and countercyclical buffer), the leverage ratio, and the calculation of aggregate risk-weighted exposure integrating credit risk (reg 23), market risk (reg 28/29), operational risk (reg 33), and counterparty credit risk.

sections.title: Process of corporate governance

subsections.heading: reg39.p
subsections.text: 39. Process of corporate governance

subsections.heading: reg39.1
subsections.text: (1) The board of directors of a bank is ultimately responsible for ensuring that an adequate and effective process of corporate governance, which is consistent with the nature, complexity and risk inherent in the bank's on-balance sheet and off-balance sheet activities and that responds to changes in the bank's environment and conditions, is established and maintained, provided that the board of directors may appoint supporting committees to assist it with its responsibilities.

subsections.heading: reg39.2
subsections.text: (2) The process of corporate governance referred to in subregulation (1) includes the maintenance of effective risk management and capital management by a bank.

subsections.heading: reg39.3
subsections.text: (3) The conduct of the business of a bank entails the ongoing management of risks, which may arise from the bank's on-balance sheet or off-balance sheet activities and which may include, among others, the following types of risk:

subsections.heading: reg39.3.a
subsections.text: capital risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.b
subsections.text: compliance risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.c
subsections.text: concentration risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.d
subsections.text: counterparty risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.e
subsections.text: country risk and transfer risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.f
subsections.text: credit risk, and in particular risks arising from impaired or problem assets and the bank's related impairments, provisions or reserves;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.g
subsections.text: currency risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.h
subsections.text: detection and prevention of criminal activities;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.i
subsections.text: equity risk arising from positions held in the bank's banking book;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.j
subsections.text: interest-rate risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.k
subsections.text: liquidity risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.l
subsections.text: market risk (position risk) in respect of positions held in the bank's trading book;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.m
subsections.text: operational risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.n
subsections.text: reputational risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.o
subsections.text: risk arising from exposure to a related person;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.p
subsections.text: risk arising from the outsourcing of material tasks or functions;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.q
subsections.text: risk arising from all relevant payment and settlement services, processes or systems;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.r
subsections.text: risk relating to procyclicality;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.s
subsections.text: risks arising from or related to inappropriate compensation practices for directors and executive officers;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.t
subsections.text: risks related to securitisation or resecuritisation structures;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.u
subsections.text: risks related to stress testing;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.v
subsections.text: risks related to the inappropriate valuation of instruments, assets or liabilities;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.w
subsections.text: solvency risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.x
subsections.text: strategic risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.y
subsections.text: technological risk;

subsections.heading: reg39.3.z
subsections.text:
translation risk;
(aa) any other risk regarded as material by the bank.

subsections.heading: reg39.4
subsections.text: (4) In order to achieve the objective relating to the maintenance of effective risk management and capital management envisaged in subregulation (2), every bank shall have in place comprehensive risk-management processes, practices and procedures, and board-approved policies—

subsections.heading: reg39.4.a
subsections.text: to identify;

subsections.heading: reg39.4.b
subsections.text: to measure;

subsections.heading: reg39.4.c
subsections.text: to monitor;

subsections.heading: reg39.4.d
subsections.text: to control;

subsections.heading: reg39.4.e
subsections.text: to appropriately price;

subsections.heading: reg39.4.f
subsections.text: to appropriately mitigate; and

subsections.heading: reg39.4.g
subsections.text:
to appropriately communicate or report,
among other things, the risks referred to in subregulation (3).

subsections.heading: reg39.5
subsections.text: (5) As a minimum, the risk management processes, practices, procedures and policies referred to in subregulation (4)—

subsections.heading: reg39.5.a
subsections.text: shall be adequate for the size and nature of the activities of the bank, including the bank's activities relating to risk mitigation, trading and exposure to counterparty credit risk, and shall periodically be adjusted in the light of the changing risk profile or financial strength of the bank, financial innovation or external market developments;

subsections.heading: reg39.5.b
subsections.text: shall be duly aligned with, and, where appropriate, provide specific guidance for the successful implementation of and the continued adherence to, the business strategy, goals and objectives, and the risk appetite or tolerance for risk, of the bank;

subsections.heading: reg39.5.c
subsections.text: shall duly specify relevant limits and allocated capital relating to the bank's various risk exposures;

subsections.heading: reg39.5.d
subsections.text: shall be sufficiently robust to: (i) determine and monitor the total indebtedness of any person to whom the bank granted credit; (ii) ensure that the bank raises appropriate and timely credit impairments and maintains adequate allowances or reserves for potential losses in respect of its loans or advances; (iii) identify and manage material interrelationships between the bank's relevant risk exposures; (iv) ensure the bank's continued compliance with the relevant documented set of internal policies, controls and procedures; (v) ensure that the bank captures the economic substance and not merely the legal form of the bank's various exposures to risk; (vi) ensure that the bank conducts sufficiently robust and independent due diligence in respect of the bank's respective investment in or exposure to instruments, products or markets; (vii) ensure that the bank regularly conducts appropriate stress-testing or scenario analysis; (viii) ensure that the bank maintains sufficient liquidity and capital adequacy buffers to remain solvent during prolonged periods of financial market stress and illiquidity; (ix) clearly delineate accountability and all relevant lines of authority across the bank's various business units, lines or activities; (x) ensure that all relevant risk management, control and business units or lines appropriately review and assess proposed new activities, investment in new instruments or the introduction of new products; (xi) ensure that the bank is able to appropriately aggregate or consolidate all relevant risks or exposure to risk; (xii) ensure ongoing, accurate, appropriate and timely communication or reporting of the bank's relevant risk exposures and any material deviation from approved policies, processes or procedures to the senior management and the board of directors; (xiii) ensure that the bank's board of directors and senior management receive timely and appropriate information regarding the condition of the bank's respective asset portfolios, including matters related to the relevant classification of credit exposure, the level of impairment or provisioning, and major problem assets; (xiv) enable the proactive management of all relevant risks; (xv) ensure that any breach of an internal limit is duly escalated and addressed.

sections.title: Guidelines relating to conduct of directors
sections.summary: Sets out guidelines for the conduct of directors of a bank or controlling company, including requirements for fiduciary duties, avoidance of conflicts of interest, and adherence to the bank's code of conduct, aligned with section 60 of the Banks Act and the King Code of Corporate Governance principles.

sections.title: Composition of the board of directors of a bank or controlling company
sections.summary: Prescribes requirements for board composition including the minimum proportion of independent non-executive directors, the establishment of board committees (audit, risk, remuneration, and social and ethics), and the requirement that the chairperson of the board be an independent non-executive director.

sections.title: Public disclosure
sections.summary: Requires banks to make prescribed Pillar 3 disclosures on a semi-annual or annual basis covering capital structure, capital adequacy, risk exposures (credit, market, operational, interest rate, liquidity, equity), remuneration practices, and leverage; disclosures must be published on the bank's website or in an easily accessible format within 90 days after the relevant period-end.

sections.title: Annual financial statements
sections.summary: Requires every bank to prepare annual financial statements in accordance with IFRS as adopted in South Africa, to have such statements audited by a registered auditor approved by the Registrar, and to submit the statements to the Registrar within 90 days after year-end together with the auditor's report.

sections.title: Audit reports
sections.summary: Prescribes the content and timing of audit reports to be submitted to the Registrar by a bank's external auditor, including reporting on the prescribed returns, internal controls, and compliance with the Banks Act and these Regulations, with the auditor required to communicate directly with the Registrar on material irregularities or reportable offences.

sections.title: Internal audit
sections.summary: Requires every bank to establish and maintain an independent internal audit function with a charter approved by the board, reporting to the audit committee, with sufficient resources and scope to provide assurance on the effectiveness of internal controls, risk management, and compliance across all material business activities.

sections.title: Compliance function
sections.summary: Requires every bank to establish an independent compliance function responsible for identifying, assessing, and monitoring compliance risk arising from the bank's failure to comply with applicable laws, regulations, and supervisory requirements, with the compliance officer reporting directly to the board or a board committee.

sections.title: Application forms and certificates of registration
sections.summary: Prescribes the prescribed application forms for obtaining a banking licence, certificates of registration for new branches, and notifications of material changes, referencing the list of forms in regulation 53 and the review procedure in regulation 54.

sections.title: Application for permission to acquire shares in a bank or controlling company
sections.summary: Sets out the procedure for obtaining the Registrar's permission under section 37 of the Banks Act to acquire a qualifying holding (10% or more of shares or voting rights) in a bank or controlling company, including the information required, fit-and-proper assessment criteria, and the Registrar's decision-making process.

sections.title: Fees payable
sections.summary: Prescribes the fees payable to the Registrar for processing applications (banking licence, branch registration, share-acquisition permission) and for the annual licence fee, with amounts determined by the Minister of Finance by notice in the Gazette from time to time.
